criteria.criterion: A status.rs unit test builds fixture records with 51 planned dispatched jobs, 28 landed, and asserts the measures (landed 28, planned 51, share about 0.549, cost per landed job, first-round accept rate) and a breach verdict because the share is below 0.64. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: The test keep_rule_flags_28_landed_of_51_planned_as_a_breach_with_the_measures passed. It asserts planned 51 and landed 28, a share of 28/51, a total cost of $51, a cost per landed job of 51/28, a first-round result of 20 accepted out of 51 (rate 20/51), and the verdict Breach. The fixture is built from records through keep_rule(&Records), so the figures are computed rather than hard-coded.

criteria.criterion: Fixture tests cover the rule's branches: at most 30 planned jobs with share at or above 0.64 reads keep; below 0.64 reads breach; at 100 or more planned jobs, share at least 0.72 with cost per landed job at most $2.50 reads keep, share at or below 0.64 reads turn off, otherwise inconclusive; zero landed gives no division by zero. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: Both branch tests passed (early_branches and decision_branches_at_100_planned_jobs). With 30 jobs, 20 landed reads keep and 19 reads breach; exactly 0.64 (16 of 25) reads keep. With 100 jobs, 72 landed at $1.39 per landed job reads keep, 72 landed at $2.78 reads inconclusive, 64 landed reads turn off and 65 reads inconclusive. The test with_nothing_landed passed: cost per landed job is None, the JSON value is null, and an empty Records gives None.

criteria.criterion: A display.rs test shows the rendered status text contains the measures with their numbers (28 of 51, 55%, baseline 64%, cost per landed job, first-round accept rate) and a breach line when breached, and no breach line when kept. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli.
criteria.evidence: The test keep_rule_lines_show_the_measures_and_a_breach_line_only_when_breached passed. It checks for the text '28 of 51 planned jobs landed (55%)', 'baseline 64%', 'cost per landed job $3.57' and 'first-round accept rate 50% (20 of 40)'. It checks that the BREACH line carries 28 of 51, 55% and 64%, that the turn-off wording appears, that the keep case has no BREACH line, and that missing values show as n/a. status() appends keep_rule_lines whenever v.keep_rule is Some.

criteria.criterion: The StatusView serialization (what `athena status --json` prints) contains a keep-rule object with the measures and verdict; a test asserts the JSON keys and values. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: StatusView has a new field, `keep_rule: Option<KeepRule>`, with derived Serialize. It is skipped only when None. The 51-job test serializes the KeepRule and asserts planned=51, landed=28, baseline_share=0.64, verdict="breach", share≈0.549, and that cost_per_landed_usd and first_round_accept_rate are floats. The test serializes the KeepRule on its own, not the whole StatusView; see the minor finding. Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` run passed.

criteria.criterion: The denominator counts planned dispatched jobs, a job stopped in planning counts as not landed, and cost per landed job divides all cost of those jobs by landed jobs, as section 9 defines it; the thresholds (30, 100, 64%, 72%, $2.50) are named constants citing job-planning.md section 9 and D110.
criteria.evidence: The filter in keep_rule() keeps jobs that have at least one plan and either a job record or a planning stop that was not accepted. Landed means JobState::Closed(Landed). Cost per landed job is the sum of spent_usd over the planned jobs divided by landed. The stopped-in-planning test passed: 2 planned, 1 landed, cost per landed job $2.0. The constants KEEP_RULE_EARLY_JOBS, KEEP_RULE_DECISION_JOBS, KEEP_RULE_BASELINE_SHARE, KEEP_RULE_TARGET_SHARE and KEEP_RULE_COST_CEILING_USD each have a doc comment citing job-planning.md section 9 and D110. All of this matches section 9 as I read it at lines 232–243.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the keep-rule evaluation in status.
criteria.evidence: Under Unreleased > Added, a new entry describes the measures, the BREACH line, the thresholds, the `keep_rule` key in --json, and that the rule only reports.

criteria.criterion: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree all passed: fmt, clippy with -D warnings, and the test suite (1359 tests).

findings.summary: The JSON test serializes the KeepRule on its own, not the StatusView that `athena status --json` prints.
findings.evidence: The test calls serde_json::to_value(&rule), not serde_json::to_value(&StatusView). The `keep_rule` field and its key name come from the derive, so the risk is low. Still, nothing tests the top-level `keep_rule` key directly.

findings.summary: The early breach rule runs from 30 up to 99 planned jobs, which section 9 does not state.
findings.evidence: keep_verdict uses `planned < KEEP_RULE_DECISION_JOBS` for the early rule, and KEEP_RULE_EARLY_JOBS is defined but never used in the logic. The constant's doc comment and the CHANGELOG explain the choice. It is a reasonable reading, since section 9 says nothing about 30 to 100 jobs, but the code does not apply the 30 threshold as such.

findings.summary: A planned job that is dispatched but still running counts in the denominator as not landed, which can understate the share while jobs are in flight.
findings.evidence: The filter keeps any planned job that has a job record. Landed requires Closed(Landed), so an open job lowers the share until it closes. Section 9's baseline (152 of 237) reads as closed outcomes. No test covers an open job.

summary: The change does what the request asks. `athena status` now works out the job-planning keep rule from the records instead of using a hard-coded figure. It counts planned jobs that were dispatched, and a job stopped in planning counts as not landed. It shows how many landed and the share, the 64% baseline, the cost per landed job and the first-round accept rate. When the rule is breached, or says to turn planning off, it adds a BREACH line with the numbers. The same measures and verdict are in `--json` under `keep_rule`. I ran the new tests in both crates and all of them pass: 5 in athena-core and 1 in athena-cli. They cover the 28-of-51 breach case, every branch of the rule, both edges of the thresholds, and a run where nothing landed, which gives no NaN or infinity. For fmt, clippy and the full test suite I relied on Athena's recorded runs, which all passed; I did not rerun them. The design document was listed as a deliverable but was not changed. The request's out-of-scope list forbids changing it, so I do not count that as a finding. I have three minor findings. The JSON test serializes the keep-rule object directly rather than the whole status view. The early rule now runs from 30 up to 100 planned jobs; the rule is silent on that range, and the change documents the choice. A planned job that is still running counts as not landed.
